sources.entry: Claude Code Repos Index by Daniel Rosehill - This is either the work of a prolific genius, or a very clever bot (or both), although it hardly matters because the quality is so good - an index of 75+ Claude Code repositories published by the author - and I'm not talking about slop. CMS, system design, deep research, IoT, agentic workflows, server management, personal health... If you spot the lie,

summary.one_liner: A curated index README by Daniel Rosehill that catalogs his many Claude Code projects (agent workspaces, plugins, CLAUDE.md patterns, MCP tooling, slash commands) organized by use case, with links to a plugin marketplace and docs portal.
summary.what_it_does: This is an index of the author's Claude Code repositories rather than a single tool. It groups entries into sections such as Systems Administration, Productivity, Legal, Health & Wellbeing, Financial Planning, Research, Argument and Perspective Exploration, Context and Personalization, Multi-Agent Tooling, MCP, Plugins, Slash Commands, and Ideas & WIP. Each entry is a one-line description of a repo, typically a "workspace" (a repo set up as a self-contained environment for one activity) or a template, plugin, or slash command. The README states that tooling has been consolidated into 28 cluster plugins that ship domain commands, skills and agents and provision project scaffolds on demand. It also recommends installing a "marketplace-guide" plugin as a starting point for browsing the marketplace.
use_cases: Finding a Claude Code workspace for a specific domain such as sysadmin, legal, or finance
Browsing examples of CLAUDE.md and context-file patterns
Discovering MCP server collections and configuration patterns
Looking for slash command and plugin ideas for Claude Code
Using Claude Code for non-software tasks like purchase research or writing
how_to_run: Browse the index README by section or use the online browse page
Install the recommended starting point: /plugin install marketplace-guide@danielrosehill
Ask Claude Code 'what's in the marketplace?' or 'is there a plugin for X?'
Install a cluster plugin for a domain and ask Claude Code to provision a scaffold
stack: Ansible (mentioned as a comparison in one entry)
notable: Organized by use case across many domains beyond software development, including homelab, legal, health, and finance
Describes an 'Agent Workspace' pattern where a git repo is a self-contained environment for an activity
Consolidated into 28 cluster plugins, each bundling commands, skills, agents and MCP configs
Includes a 'Claude Context Analysis' and several CLAUDE.md context-management patterns
Author states it is human-designed and refined, generated with Claude Code
caveats: Most entries are one-line descriptions; many are early, WIP, stubs or placeholders (the README has an Ideas & WIP section saying so)
Many sections point to separate dedicated sub-pages for full lists (for example 187 plugins and 13 research entries), which were not included in this README
Some repositories are described as concepts or plans rather than working tools
